processinfo.head: Processing Information note
processinfo.p: The following collection was integrated into this subseries: Lithuanian American Activity and Organizations (TAM 132.23)

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: The Association of Lithuanian Workers, or LDS (Lietuviu Darbininku Susivienijimas), was founded in 1930 as a fraternal organization politically oriented toward the CPUSA. From 1953 to 1957 the LDS was on the U.S. Attorney General's list of subversive organizations. As of 2003, the LDS continued to administer an insurance program, and in 2006 the LDS was merged into the Royal Arcanum, a non-ethnically-based fraternal organization. Although founded in New York, the bulk of the subseries derives from the organization's activity in Chicago and its environs, where Lithuanian American radicalism was centered. This subseries holds some correspondence, notably between the U.S. Attorney General's office and Jacob Pauliukas, the editor of the LDS' Chicago Lithuanian language newspaper Vilnis. There are also files on allied Lithuanian American progressive organizations and on Lithuanian World War II war criminals. Some scrapbooks are also in this subseries, including two which pertain to the life and work of Sophie Kaross, a Lithuanian American Communist. Much of the material is in Lithuanian.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This subseries is arranged alphabetically by youth organization name.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: In 2017, select audio and video recordings previously part of the Communist Party of the United States of America Audio Collection (TAM 132.001) were incorporated into subseries V.C and were integrated into the file arrangement.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: Subseries C consists of records from several youth organizations affiliated with the Communist Party at the national and local level. These youth organizations began appearing in the early 1920s and continued to form or reform throughout the 20th century; the Young Communist League (YCL) and the Young Workers Liberation League (YWLL) are perhaps the most well-known. The records of the Young Communist League make up the bulk of the subseries. Records from the first incarnation of the Young Communist League (1922-1943) are present; however, the majority of the YCL's records document their activities following its reformation in 1983. Records detailing the activities of the W.E.B. Du Bois Clubs of America and the Labor Youth League are also available in this subseries. These records include correspondence, educational materials, essays, reports, notes, meeting minutes, and organizing materials as well as select audio and video recordings from YCL and YWLL conventions, meetings, rallies, and educational programs.

An accretion of Young Communist League records was added to this series in 2018. These materials include pamphlets and ephemera from youth festivals, National Convention organizing files, drafts and articles from the publication Dialog, and a small amount of correspondence. They also include many unprocessed digital files on several CD-R, DVD-R, and floppy disks containing digital images, administrative files, presentations, reports, articles, and discussion drafts dated from 1996 to 2009.

did.unittitle: Subseries V.D. Los Angeles Committee on Unemployment

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries consists of documentation of the Los Angeles Committee on Employment, which sought to "assist the unemployed in settling grievances with the unemployment insurance office and welfare agencies," supported trade unions, and worked to fight discrimination in housing and employment. The group, possibly a CPUSA surrogate organization, or affiliated with the CPUSA, is documented in this folder through flyers, correspondence, a handbook, and press releases.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: All subseries are arranged chronologically.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: In 2017, select audio and video recordings previously part of the Communist Party of the United States of America Audio Collection (TAM 132.001) were incorporated into subseries VI.A and were integrated into the file arrangement. Video recordings from the Communist Party Non-Print Collection (TAM 132.003) were also added to subseries VI.A. Two audio tapes were added to subseries VI.B. A scrapbook and poster mock-ups from the People Before Profits campaign from the Communist Party Non-Print Collection were added to subseries VI.C.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: Several prominent members of the Communist Party, USA campaigned for public office on the CPUSA ticket at all levels of government throughout the 20th century. Records produced during many of those candidacies, such as internal working documents and public distribution materials, can be found in this series. The first subseries documents campaigns for President of the United States, including bids by party leaders William Z. Foster, Earl Browder, and Gus Hall. Subseries B provides materials from national and state elections across the United States, while Subseries C focuses on records originating from New York state and city elections.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: Records contained in this subseries document the United States presidential campaigns of members running on the Communist Party, USA ticket. The bulk of the series is devoted to Gus Hall's four presidential bids during the 1970s and 1980s, though some records from the campaigns of William Z. Foster, Earl Browder (1930s-40s), and Charlene Mitchell (1968) are also included. Hall's 1976 campaign with party member Jarvis Tyner as candidate for Vice President and his 1984 campaign with party member Angela Davis as his running mate are most extensively represented. Materials include correspondence, distribution materials, meeting minutes, research notes and speech drafts, and mainly focus on campaign strategic planning. Audio and video recordings of rallies and events for the Hall/Tyner and Hall/Davis presidential campaigns are also well represented in this subseries. They provide records of the Party's public efforts as well as internal Party meetings related to campaigns.

Subseries VI.B: National and State Elections

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: This small subseries holds records detailing Communist Party participation in and reaction to national and state elections; it also includes some materials from other minor political parties, including the American Labor and Progressive parties. Noteworthy materials include the several versions of the Communist Party election platform and a variety of distribution materials and strategic planning notes from the 1920s and 1930s. Other materials in this subseries include 2 audio recordings of regional campaign rallies, and several photographs from unidentified local campaigns.

Subseries VI.C: New York City, State, and Congressional Elections

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: This subseries documents the city and state public office campaigns of members of the Communist Party of New York, as well as the work of the New York Committee to Elect Communist Candidates in the 1970s. Materials originating from Charlene Mitchell's 1988 bid for United States Senator can be found in this subseries; a small amount of material from the campaigns of some well-known party members, including Benjamin Davis and Simon Gerson are also present. Transcripts of the speeches delivered by Elizabeth Gurley Flynn, Robert Minor, and Earl Browder at a 1942 election rally at Madison Square Garden are particularly notable, as are copies of distribution materials from the 1930s.

Series VII: Trials and Legal Records

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: This series is divided into three subseries and consists of records detailing legal trials which involved the CPUSA as an organization, as well as individual members and associated persons and organizations. Though much of the material originates from the local, state, and federal US court systems, there are some items which were generated from the CPUSA itself.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: The first subseries is the most substantial; it documents several notable trials involving members of the CPUSA and associated individuals and organizations who were prosecuted under the 1940 Smith Act, including Joseph Brandt, Eugene Dennis (also represented by his trial for contempt of court, arising from his Smith Act trial), Elizabeth Gurley Flynn, and Stephen Mesarosh (Steve Nelson). Many cases began at the local or state level and progressed to the federal court system. Transcripts, trial exhibits, and background research for several of these cases are available here. Of particular interest are two boxes of index cards which provide biographical information on a number of individuals who acted as government witnesses, as well as details about the cases in which they gave testimony.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: Files found in the second subseries reflect trials that resulted from a variety of prosecutions, including perjury, contempt, and deportation hearings. Individuals are either CPUSA members or individuals associated with the organization, including William Albertson, Harry Bridges, Gerhart Eisler, Charlene Mitchell, Morris Schappes and Louis Weinstock, as well as files from the New York Supreme Court, relating to the Inquiry by the Board of Regents with Regard to the CPUSA

Subseries VII.C: Legal Documents and Legislation

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: This subseries holds legal documents concerning several federal laws enacted during the 1940s and 1950s, such as the McCarran Act and the Smith Act, and New York State's Feinberg Law, under which CPUSA members were prosecuted. It also holds files originating from the CPUSA regarding protest and activism in reaction to these laws. Records and reports from US congressional committees, like the House Committee on Un-American Activities (generally known as the House Un-American Activities Committee or HUAC), can also be found here. There are also two scrapbooks on various communist trials.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: The Communist Party, USA issued a number of theoretical and informational publications of varying frequency at the national and local level. Administrative records from some of the better known publications are included in this series, as well as a large volume of clippings from the Party newspaper. Some materials from the publishing branch of the CPUSA, the International Publishers, Co., are also present.

did.unittitle: Subseries VIII.A: People's Weekly World Administrative Records

processinfo.head: Processing Information note
processinfo.p: The following collection was integrated into this subseries: Joseph North Papers (TAM 132.08)

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: The newspaper of the CPUSA began as the Daily Worker in 1924. It went through several incarnations over the course of the 20th century, including the Worker, the Daily World, the People's Daily World, and the People's Weekly World; in 2009 the newspaper became the People's World, published in an online format. This subseries contains the newspaper's administrative records, the bulk of which derive from the 1970s, 1980s, and 1990s. Article drafts, correspondence, and staff files can be found here, including subject files complied by individual staff members, mostly notably Joseph North, and also Grace and Ted Bassett, Marylin Bechtel, William Dennison, Ben Riskin, William Weinstone, Carl Winter, and Mike Zagarell.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: This subseries holds a selection of clipping files from the Party's newspaper. The majority of clippings originate from 1968-1986 when the paper was known as the Daily World; a small amount of clippings are from its predecessors, the Daily Worker (1924-1958) and the Worker (1958-1968), and from its successors, the People's Daily World (1986-1990) and the People's Weekly World (1990-2009). Clippings are organized into three sub-subseries: state Communist Party organizations; labor unions and labor organizations; and individuals, organizations, and topics.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: The bulk of this subseries is devoted to records from International Publishers, Co. a publishing arm of the CPUSA, and from Political Affairs (formerly The Communist), a theoretical journal affiliated with the Party. Materials from International Publishers consist of correspondence to and from staff editors, including some correspondence of Alexander Trachtenberg, company founder. Records from Political Affairs are more varied, offering article drafts, correspondence, and files of various editors from the 1980s and 1990s, notably Joe Simms..

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: Series IX contains personal papers and manuscripts created by CPUSA members and individuals aligned with the Party. They provide unique documentation of the lives of CPUSA leaders as well as its rank and file, and demonstrate how the political lives of these individuals were often intertwined with their personal lives.

processinfo.head: Processing Information note
processinfo.p: The following collections were integrated into this subseries: Elizabeth Gurley Flynn (TAM 132.05); James W. Ford Papers (TAM 132.06); Robert Minor Papers (TAM 132.07); Paul Robeson Clippings and Printed Ephemera (TAM 132.09); Charles Emil Ruthenberg: Letters from Rachele Ragozin (TAM 132.10); Jim West: 70 Years of Communist Activism, Memoirs (TAM 132.13); Henry Winston Prison Correspondence and Miscellaneous Papers (TAM 132.14); Lester Cole Correspondence (TAM 132.15); Eugene Dennis Prison Letters (TAM 132.16); Rose Baron, Letters Received (TAM 132.19); William L. Patterson Correspondence and Writings (TAM 132.24); and in 2013, the W.E.B. Du Bois Photographs Collection (PHOTOS 238). The majority of the photographs were added to this series in 2017 from the Communist Party Non Print Collection (TAM 132.003). Many of these photographs had been removed from the papers of individuals in the Party and grouped in alphabetical order. In some cases, photographs were grouped together in folders by last name within an alphabetical range, while others folders contained the photographs of a single individual. Folders have been integrated into this series alphabetically. Other photographs that were loose in boxes and roughly grouped by individual were also added to this series. Not all of these photographs correspond to a set of personal papers, but they have nonetheless been integrated into this series alphabetically by individual last name.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: In an attempt to preserve Party history, the CPUSA's History Commission began asking members to donate their personal papers to the national office during the early 1980s. These papers formed the original CPUSA Archives and were cared for by the Reference Center for Marxist Studies. They are now part of this subseries, in addition to other personal papers that were preserved over the years at Party headquarters in New York City. This subseries holds a rich historical significance, not only in its documentation of the Party, but also because it illustrates how members applied communist principles to their lives and work outside the CPUSA. Almost every individual represented here played a pivotal role in the history of communism in the United States, including Angela Davis, Elizabeth Gurley Flynn, John Ford, and Paul Robeson. These papers take a variety of forms—correspondence, essays, reference and research notes, scrapbooks, photographs, and personal memorabilia. The prison correspondence of Charles E. Ruthenberg, Robert Minor (1930 NYC unemployed demonstration) and General Secretary Eugene Dennis and Henry Winston (Smith Act) can also be found here. In an attempt to highlight items that originate from lesser known Party members or that document the early 20th century personal lives of particular members, researchers are pointed to the papers of Mary Gale, longtime Communist and ILGWU member; the personal materials of Lottie Blumenthal Gordon which document her early work life and lifetime dedication to the Party; and the correspondence, writings, the correspondence of Rose Baron of the International Labor Defense and the International Red Aid, and personal items of cartoonist and journalist Robert Minor which demonstrate Minor's rich public and private life. Photographs added to this series in 2017 include images of notable Party members at rallies and demonstrations, portraits, personal photos, and albums. Photos documenting Henry Winston's travels as a foreign delegate are most extensive. Other photos feature Party members including Angela Davis, Eugene Denis, Elizabeth Gurley Flynn, John Ford, and William Foster among others, and span the early 1910s-1980s. Also included in this series are several photo albums of unidentified individuals. Albums depict families and travels to Soviet satellite states, but the individuals featured in them are unidentified.

processinfo.head: Processing Information note
processinfo.p: The following collection was integrated into this subseries: W.E.B. Du Bois' A Soliloquy on Viewing my Life from the Last Decade of its First Century and Publishing Correspondence (TAM 132.03). The personal names which appear in parentheses following manuscript titles with an unknown author indicate the probable author.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: This subseries is made up of manuscripts and drafts written by numerous Party members or individuals aligned with the CPUSA. These writings touch on a variety of issues and interests such as the experience of African Americans, like W.E.B. Du Bois, James West (at one time leader of the Indiana CP, and of the Central Review Commission) the work of labor organizers, and the history of communism in the United States. Like the prior subseries, these manuscripts make explicit the connections members drew between communist ideology and their lives outside official Party work. Manuscripts take several forms including poetry, theatrical scripts, biographical sketches, historical essays, and memoirs.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: This series contains files on individuals, organizations, and topics that were compiled by Communist Party, USA members, presumably for reference purposes. Notable is the Subseries B. Biographical Files on Communist Activists and Leaders.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Each subseries is made up of a discrete collection of files that are arranged according to their original order with the exception of subseries E and F. The archivist imposed an alphabetical arrangement on the files in subseries E and F in the absence of original order.

did.unittitle: Subseries X.A: Activists and Organizations Subject Files

processinfo.head: Processing Information note
processinfo.p: The following collection was integrated into this subseries: Progressive Activists and Organizations Subject Files (TAM 132.12)

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: Much of the activity of the Communist Party took place in the context of working within mass organizations; those established by the Party were often referred to as front organizations. Mass organizations were usually devoted to a single issue or constituency and had a broader membership and political appeal than the explicitly radical Communist Party. This strategy, known as popular front politics, sought broad alliances with leftists around a minimum reform program as opposed to a maximum radical or revolutionary program, in the hope of moving broad masses of people to the left. This subseries was likely compiled by the History Commission. Folders principally contain clippings, printed ephemera, and some internal Party documents. Notable individuals represented include Harry Bridges, Benjamin Gitlow, Dorothy Healy, folksinger Pete Seeger, and Henry Wallace. Popular front organizations represented include the Civil Rights Congress, International Labor Defense, League of American Writers, Southern Negro Youth Congress, and Workshop for People's Art.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: This subseries contains biographical material on rank and file communist activists and CPUSA leaders. There are also several files on notable progressives not known or thought to be Communists. While the majority of the files consist of clippings and printed ephemera, some contain correspondence, biographical and autobiographical typescripts, oral history interview transcripts, various documents relating to civil liberties cases, and memorabilia. Phil Bart, onetime head of the Party's History Commission, is the principal correspondent; he may have been responsible for the compilation of this collection.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: Philip Bart was a longtime Communist Party member and official. He served as the Party's Organizational Secretary (ca. 1963), and as the head of the History Commission (ca. 1979). The majority of this collection consists of clippings from the Communist Party Press, namely the Daily Worker, the Worker, and the Daily World, along with clippings from other periodicals. There is also a small amount of printed ephemera. Materials in this subseries focus on the growth of anti-communism after World War II, the political and legal attacks on the Communist Party and its members, the role of the House Un-American Activities Committee and the Subversive Activities Control Board, and the U.S. government's loyalty oath program.

processinfo.p: The following collection was integrated into this subseries: Middle East Clippings Files (TAM 132.20)

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: The CPUSA closely followed events in the Middle East, was strongly critical of Israel and its relations with its Arab neighbors, and hoped that socialism would become the predominant current in the Arab world. The collection contains clippings from the New York Times, the International Herald Tribune, and other leading mainstream newspapers, covering domestic and foreign politics in the Middle East, with a particular emphasis on Egypt and its short-lived union with Syria, the United Arab Republic.

Series XI: Broadcasts and Public Events

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This series is arranged into five subseries by topic or function. Each series contains recordings that document different types of events or public broadcasts. Recordings contained within subseries are arranged alphabetically by title. Titles were derived from annotations on media carriers and in some cases may be inconsistent. Recordings in subseries XI.E: Broadcasts are arranged alphabetically by program title and listed ascending in order by episode number.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains audio and video recordings of Communist Party and Party affiliated meetings, lectures, public events, celebrations, broadcasts, and appearances of Party leaders in national media. Recordings in the first three subseries date from the 1950s to the 1990s and feature recordings of lectures, discussions, rallies, and public events. These recordings provide an extensive record of the public and political debates that the Party was engaged in during those years. Broadcast recordings feature tapes of radio and television programs produced by the Party, and feature recordings of three programs, Gus Hall's radio Update, and the television programs People Before Profits, and Changing America.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: Materials in this series were added to the collection in 2017. Audio recordings were previously included in the Communist Party of the United States Audio Collection (TAM 132.001) and were arranged by format. Videos were not previously arranged. Video tapes were inventoried and have been arranged into sub-series along with audio recordings by the archivist.

did.unittitle: Subseries XI.A: Forums, Meetings, and Lectures

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries contains over 1600 audio and video recordings of lectures, forums, conference panels, and class discussions on socialist ideology, Marxist theory, and current events. The bulk of the recordings are contained on audio cassette and feature lectures by Party leaders including Gus Hall, Herbert Aptheker, James Jackson, Jarvis Tyner, George Meyers, and Angela Davis among others. This subseries includes recordings from conferences on special topics like Marxism and culture, black liberation, the working class, and socialism. Conference recordings featured in this series differ from National Party Conventions and Conferences in Series I and Series II, which set official Party policy. Instead, conference recordings in this subseries focus on ideological discussion and education.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries features recordings of public statements made by Communist Party leaders or public demonstrations supported by the Party. They include audio and video recordings of rallies and demonstrations, festivals, press release statements from Party leadership, and interviews and speeches by Communist Party members. Speeches by long-time Communist Party Chairman Gus Hall are featured prominently in this subseries, as are tapes of May Day rallies between the 1970s and 1990s.

Subseries XI.D: Radio and Television Appearances

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries contains recordings of radio and television appearances by members of the Communist Party. Between the early 1950s to the late 1990s Party members were frequently interviewed on radio and TV. Recordings feature media appearances as well as variety of Communist Party campaign materials, which aired in support of Gus Hall and Jarvis Tyner's campaigns during the 1972 and 1976 Presidential elections as well as for Gus Hall and Angela Davis' 1980 and 1984 election campaigns. Audio from radio and television documentaries recorded by Party members are also included in this series.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries contains recordings of television and radio programs produced by the Communist Party. It primarily consists of recordings of three shows: the radio program Update, and the television shows People Before Profits and Changing America. Update was recorded by Communist Party Chairman Gus Hall beginning in 1985. Hall produced weekly cassette recordings discussing national and worldwide political trends. These recordings were played at the start of Secretariat and Political Bureau meetings and were also distributed to District Organizers and Clubs. The recordings were intended for internal Communist Party, USA membership and were used as a link between the national organization and district bodies. People Before Profits was a political talk show created by the Communist Party's Video Department beginning in the mid-1980s and running until 1990. The program was produced by the Party and sent to local and public access television stations across the United States. Changing America was the successor to People Before Profits, and ran between 1999 and 2000. Recordings of Changing America and Update contain almost complete runs of each program, with only a few missing episodes, and largely consist of completed episodes. Recordings of the talk show People Before Profits are less clearly labeled, contain many overlapping episode numbers, and fragments of episodes. These programs show the ways in which the Communist Party reacted to current political issues and the ways the Party shared its stance on issues with rank and file members and the public. Unidentified fragments of program recordings are also included in this subseries. Although the programs for which they were created is unidentified they most likely relate to either People Before Profits or Changing America.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains an assortment of photographs, posters, buttons, and artifacts created and collected by the Communist Party of the United States and by Party members. Many of the items in this series commemorate events and document political issues or topics that were of interest to the Party. Buttons and posters document a variety of political and social issues, while photographs and artifacts provide documentation of regional Party activities, specific events, or groups associated with the CPUSA. Materials in this series were collected from a variety of sources and touch on a wide array of topics, some of which may not be directly related to Communist Party activity.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: Photographs in this subseries were originally included as part of the Communist Party, USA Non-Print Collection (TAM 132.003). They had been previously grouped by format with photographs of individuals, which have been placed Subseries IX.A: Individuals, Personal Papers. A small portion of photographs were arranged topically prior to processing in 2017, but the bulk were in loose grouping and have been arranged topically by the archivist.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Photographs in this series contain images of public demonstrations, affiliated groups, and collected photographs on a wide variety of topics. Photographs of events and demonstrations document Communist Party regional activities, as well as activities of labor groups and other organization on the political left. Photographs in this subseries were both collected, rather than produced, by the CPUSA, and provide a glimpse into the array of topics of interest to the Party. Among these materials are collected prints created by various photographers documenting topics like rural life in Latin America, working-class people in New York City, and labor demonstrations. Other photographs document events in communist nations including the Soviet Union, North Korea, China, and Eastern European Soviet satellite nations. Images documenting CPUSA activities include images of Party leaders, meetings, and various demonstrations.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries consists of over 300 posters dating from the 1930s to the present, with the bulk dating from the 1970s to the present. The subseries documents a diverse array of topics of interest to the international Communist movement, including domestic and international political issues, Communist history, labor organizing, and solidarity movements. There are a significant number of posters produced by the CPUSA, the Communist Party of Portugal, the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, the French Communist Party and the General Confederation of Labour (CGT), as well as posters created by a range of organizations and individuals. There are a significant number of posters produced for the annual World Youth and Students Festival. The posters in this subseries include a diverse array of graphic styles and production techniques. These posters place the CPUSA within the context of worldwide Communist organizing, and are particularly strong on international political issues.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: The Communist Party of the United States Poster and Graphics Collection (GRAPHICS.024) was added the the Communist Party Records as subseries XII.B: Posters in 2017. Posters in this series have not been rearranged and follow the previous arrangement of GRAPHICS.024.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The subseries is arranged alphabetically by topic or region, with sub-topics when appropriate. Folder-level description includes a scope and contents note describing additional topics, people, places featured in the posters. This information is derived from the images and text from the posters in each folder. Date ranges are approximate, and are based on information from the posters in each folder.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries consists of hundreds of buttons and political badges dating from the 1910s to 1990s. Buttons were both collected and created by the CPUSA and document a wide array of political topics and election campaigns. A large portion of the buttons relate to election campaigns, and feature CPUSA candidates at the state and national level as well as buttons in support of candidates not affiliated with the Communist Party. Political badges feature small pins dating from the 1920s and 1940s, which touch on topics such as participation in May Day demonstrations, political causes, labor affiliation, and Party support. They also include pins in support of early CPUSA political candidates. Other buttons document a broad range of political topics from the 1950s to early 2000s, including anti-capitalism, environmentalism, peace, civil rights, women's rights, and campaigns against political leaders in the United States.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: Buttons in this subseries were processed in 2017. At the time of processing, buttons were loose in boxes with no clear arrangement. Buttons have been arranged roughly by topic and attached foam boards. A small set of political badges and May Day pins were grouped together prior to processing and have been maintained in their original groupings.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Buttons in this subseries are arranged into groupings by general topic, with sub-topics where necessary. Because some topics overlap, buttons contained in topical groupings may also relate to other topics contained in this subseries.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries is comprised of an assortment of collected items relating to party events, individual members, or affiliated groups. It includes a wide array of materials such as banners, flags, t-shirts, political stickers, postage stamps, ink stamps, stationery, flyers, badges, and ribbons. Memorabilia related to youth activities are prominently featured among these materials and include textile banners, pennants, arm bands, hats, and badges. They also include poster boards filled with images documenting youth participation in the CPUSA from the 1930s to 1990s. Many items relate specifically to the Young Communist League (YCL) and Young Workers Liberation League (YWLL), but other items are more generally document youth activism in the party. Several items relate to Communist Party publications including memorabilia from the Daily World, and metal plates of text and images used in Communist Party publications between the 1940s and 1950s.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Collected artifacts in this subseries are arranged alphabetically by item name or topic.

Series XIII: Collected Film and Audio Library

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains film reels, video tapes, audio cassettes, video reels, and vinyl records collected by the Communist Party of the United States. Audio recordings in this series consist predominantly of labor and protest songs, which are performed by a variety of artists. Other audio recordings contain educational content including history lessons on Karl Marx and World War II, and English-Russian phrases. Films make up the bulk of this series and consists of collected international documentaries and television programs, the majority of which were created in the Soviet Union. Other films in this series were collected from a wide range of communist countries and are in a variety of languages including Korean, Spanish, German, Czech, Chinese, and Vietnamese. Videos include a collection of documentaries and programs on labor demonstration in the United States, progressive activism, the Cold War, and international social movements. Information about the content of films, videos, and audio recordings in this series has been derived largely from labels and annotation on the individual items. In several cases annotations provide an incomplete information, and in others the content of the recordings is unknown. These materials consist of a mixture of commercially produced and original recordings. Songs from demonstrations and performances of the "Internationale" are largely original content while other collected folk songs and lecture series materials are commercially produced. Likewise, films contain commercially produced content including foreign documentaries and television programs from the Soviet Union. A small portion of these films also contain amateur content as well.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This series is divided into 3 subseries by format. Materials within subseries are listed alphabetically by title.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries includes audio recordings collected by the Communist Party. The majority of these recordings consist of recorded folk and protest songs, including multiple recordings of the popular socialist song "The Internationale," which was adopted as the anthem of the Socialist International in the late 19th century. Other songs include recordings by notable singers such as Paul Robeson and Pete Seeger. Many recordings feature copies of commercially produced songs, while a select few feature songs performed at events like campaign rallies, youth conferences, or international festivals. Recordings are largely on audio cassette and were created between the 1980s and 1990s, but in some cases these recordings may be reproductions of older songs produced several decades earlier.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Songs are listed alphabetically by performer name. In tapes where performer is unknown songs are listed alphabetically by title.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The subseries contains 421 film reels. The bulk of the films are 16mm, but other formats include 8mm, Super 8, and 35mm. These films largely consist of exhibition prints of foreign documentaries, the majority of which are in Russian, and feature on topics regarding Soviet history and life in the Soviet Union. Most films were produced between the 1970s and 1980s, but several were produced as early as 1935. Other languages include Korean, Spanish, German, Czech, Chinese, and Vietnamese, with only a small portion of films in English. Several films include amateur footage of public events including May Day demonstrations and Communist Party election rallies. Amateur footage also features travels to socialist countries by members of the Communist Party in the 1960s, the trial of Angela Davis, and footage of election campaigns in the 1970s and 1980s. Many of these reels are poorly labeled and lack clear information about dates or content, and some cannot be identified.

Film titles have been derived from annotations on the original containers. In several cases foreign language titles were translated into English to provide more information about the content of the films. English titles are literal translations, and are followed by original titles in parenthesis.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Videos in this subseries contain an assortment of recorded events, speeches, documentaries, and television programs collected by the Communist Party. Tapes include commercially produced VHS tapes, recordings of events in which the Communist Party was interested but not directly involved, and items whose content cannot be determined by their current labels. The content of these tapes touches on a variety of issues related to labor activism and demonstrations in the United States and social issues in Africa, Latin America, Korea, and Cuba. Titles of tapes are derived from annotations on cassettes, which in many cases are unclear. These tapes have not been preservered and may be rearranged into Series XI: Broadcasts and Public Events after materials have been digitized.

Some tapes may contain off-air content, but this content cannot be identified until videos are selected for playback. Off-air materials cannot be preserved because of copyright concerns, and will be deaccessioned when identified.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Videos are arranged alphabetically by title.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content Note
scopecontent.p: The website of the Communist Party of the United States of America includes information about Party history, platform, upcoming actions and events, publications, and educational resources for local organizers. The website was first captured in 2007. Websites of Communist Party publications Political Affairs, People's Weekly World, and Labor Upfront are also included in this series. These websites include articles from the publications, which were first captured in 2008.

phystech.head: Physical Characteristics and Technical Requirements
phystech.p: Due to technical or privacy issues, archived websites may not be exact copies of the original website at the time of the web crawl. Certain file types will not be captured dependent on how they are embedded in the site. Other parts of websites that the crawler has difficulty capturing includes Javascript, streaming content, database-driven content, and highly interactive content. Full-Text searches of archived websites are available at https://archive-it.org/organizations/567.

accruals.head: Accruals
accruals.p: People's World and CPUSA websites are crawled quarterly.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Websites are arranged alphabetically then by crawl date.

did.unittitle: Communist Party of the United States of America Archived Website

daodesc.p: Communist Party USA Archived Website: October 2007-ongoing

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Communist Party USA website was first collected in late 2007. The website contained the party platform and constitution; reports and proceedings from conventions, conferences, committee meetings, and national conventions in the early 2000s; press releases; organizing around the 2008 elections; fundraising; the Manufacturing Think Tank; study and discussion guides; and news and their e-newsletter from their Organizing Department, the Party eBuilder. The website focused on many issues (called "struggles" by the CPUSA), including equality for Black, Native American, Mexican American, and Puerto Rican peoples; civil rights; culture outside of commercialism; economic democracy; public education; electoral politics; environmental protection; healthcare; immigrant rights; independent media; international communist unity; justice system reform; labor organizing; LGBTQIA+ rights; solidarity against war and imperialist globalization; protections for Social Security and Medicaid; protection from agribusiness; coalition building; and women's equality. In early 2010, the website was redesigned. The website redesign included information on their national convention held every four years; speeches; commentary; reports; their blog; an FAQ on the party platform and communism; and action campaigns and petitions related to climate change, net neutrality, Iranian sanctions and peace deal, Planned Parenthood, overtime pay threshold, free higher education, voter suppression, worker safety, protections for Medicaid and Social Security, Black Lives Matter, national budget, police brutality, and corporate interests in politics. In 2016, the website was redesigned to its current iteration (as of this writing). It contains educational resources; classes and quizzes on Marxism; their podcast, "the Specter;" "This Week @CPUSA" discussion series; events; and articles, videos, and local activities on their blog Party Voices.

appraisal.head: Appraisal
appraisal.p: Crawl was limited to domains and subdomains of digitalhuac.com and documentcloud.org in order to remain within the collection scope and data constraints.

bioghist.head: Historical Note
bioghist.p: Digital HUAC was a project by students in a Digital Humanities Praxis course at the Graduate Center, City University of New York to create a database of House of Un-American Activities Committee testimonies.

bioghist.p: The Labor Upfront Newsletter was the online publication of the Labor Commission of the Communist Party, USA, which directed the Party's work in the labor movement. The blog was active from 2007-2010.

bioghist.head: Historical Note
bioghist.p: People's World, established online in 2009, is a national news website that reports on workers' rights, peace, equality, social and economic justice, democracy, civil liberties, women's rights, protection of the environment, and other topics. The website is affiliated with the Community Party USA and descended from the Daily Worker, the Communist Party's newspaper from 1924-1991. The Spanish language edition of the website was called Neustro Mundo, later Mundo Popular.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The websites mostly contain news and opinion from the national paper and the New York district. The main People's World, website and URL changed in 2009 and redesigned in 2016. Additionally, these websites cover their fundraising efforts and videos related to testimonials, centennial celebrations, fundraising, rallies, panel discussions, COVID, unemployment, the Occupy Wall Street movement, strike footage, and other events.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Political Affairs was an online magazine of theories, ideas, politics and culture of the socialist and democratic traditions and visions of the United States from a working class point of view. The website contains sections on features, culture, editor's blog, education, podcasts, and news analysis. The website features stories from the labor movement; from the struggles of communities of color and diverse nationalities against racial injustice and inequality; and from movements of women, youth, seniors, disabled, and LGBTQIA+ communities for equality. The website was active from 2010-2015.

daodesc.p: Young Communist League USA Archived Website: September 2007-August 2016

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The website contains news listings, membership applications, their publication Dynamic Magazine, and their podcast the Specter.

bioghist.head: Historical Note
bioghist.p: The Young Communist League, USA was a multi-racial, working class organization for young members of the CPUSA. The organization's main goal is to educate members into becoming communists. They work to advocate for the working class, reject the abuse of drugs and alcohol, to fight for the equality of all young people, to end racism and discrimination, and work for peace, full employment, complete equality, trade union and democratic rights. The YCLUSA was active online from the late 1990s to 2015. They reemerged online in circa 2020.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This accretion to the Communist Party of the United States of America consists of an autobiographical manuscript written in Yiddish by Josh Wishensky with an English translation, and notebooks from the Illinois CPUSA district from 2001-2018 documenting meetings, campaigns, and social activities.
